:::caution[Superseded — the wake API was redesigned (directed-wake-honesty)]
Two parts of this runbook's wake surface no longer match the code. The
always-arm wiring, the standing-row upsert + migration 183, the `await-inbox`
annotation, the full `turn:interrupt` dual, and both EI-151 owner-scoping rungs
all still verify — only the `coord:send` wake API drifted.

- **No more `wake.warning` / `woken:0` warning.** The "woken:0 warning" section
  below used to quote a `wake.warning` string for the fired-but-woke-nobody
  case. That field is gone. A `required` wake, or an `optimistic` wake without a
  declared backstop, now reports the miss via `wake.recipient_absent: true`
  plus a `wake.note` — see the loud-miss branch in
  `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/tools/send.ts`. The
  miss is still auditable, but the surface is now `recipient_absent`, not a
  `warning` field.

- **`wake` is a union, not a boolean.** The body used to write the API as
  `coord:send {wake:true}`. `wake` is now `boolean | 'required' | 'optimistic'`
  on the `send` schema, coerced to the internal wake mode (`true → 'required'`,
  `false`/omit → no wake). Legacy `{wake:true}` still functions, but the
  documented intent surface is `wake:'required'` for a loud required wake or
  `wake:'optimistic'` when a durable `backstop:` will re-dispatch a miss.
  Without a declared backstop, an optimistic miss is reported loudly too.

See plan `directed-wake-honesty-and-spawn-handoff-2026-06-14`. The original
narrative below is preserved.
:::

## What changed

You no longer have to *remember* to make yourself wakeable. The operator now
**arms your inbox-wake watch automatically at SessionStart** — server-side, in the
lifecycle endpoint that `~/.papercusp/hooks/cc/lifecycle-report.sh` already POSTs to
(`activity:report`, `kind:lifecycle`). It is client-agnostic (claude / omp / codex)
and armed for the whole session, not just between turns. So every psu/Mug-launched
agent is re-invokable on a `coord:send {wake:'required'}` (legacy `wake:true`)
**even when it has no idea it will ever be woken**.

Plan: `turn-lifecycle-control-2026-06-08` (Phase 1, D-001). The old rule — "call
`coord:await-inbox` when you go idle or you won't be wakeable" — is dead. Forgetting
to arm no longer strands you.

## The model: one standing row per agent

Your watch is a single row in `harness_shared.event_awaits`, keyed
`(workspace_id, subscriber_id, event_key)` with `event_key = coord:inbox-wake:<you>`.

- **Idempotent (D-002).** SessionStart re-arms by **upsert** (`upsertInboxWakeAwait`,
  `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE`): re-arming refreshes the captured wake-handle + idle
  note + floor on the one row — it never inserts a duplicate. A partial unique index
  (migration 183) enforces exactly one live standing inbox-wake await per agent.
- **The rendezvous.** `coord:send {wake:'required', to:[you]}` (legacy `wake:true`)
  and `coord:message-agent`
  fires exactly `coord:inbox-wake:<you>` — a key only you watch. It is targeted,
  never a broadcast; `*`/`human` are not wakeable (no thunder-herd).
- **SessionEnd cancels it (D-003).** A clean session end cancels your standing
  watch, so a wake can't race a just-exited session and phantom-resume it. If work
  arrives later, a fresh session is spawned by whoever needs it.

## `coord:await-inbox` is now just an annotation (D-005)

Because arming is automatic, `coord:await-inbox` is **no longer the gate** that makes
you wakeable. It survives as an *annotation*: it refreshes the "why I'm idle" note on
your already-armed standing row (the note rides your wake turn) and lets you tune your
`min_sleep_sec` floor. Call it to explain your idle state if you like — but forgetting
to no longer makes you unwakeable, which was the whole point.

## You still must not poll

Always-arm makes you *reliably wakeable*; it does not make polling OK. When you have
no queued work: **end your turn.** You are re-invoked when someone `coord:send`s you
with `{wake:'required'}` (legacy `wake:true`; bursts inside your floor coalesce
into one wake). For a specific
one-shot readiness (a lock grant, a peer's artifact, a plan-run finishing) use
`events:await` on that exact key and end the turn. A wake costs a whole turn — await
only what genuinely blocks you; ambient interest stays a `topics:subscribe`.

## The woken:0 warning — don't trust a silent ok (D-010)

`coord:send {wake:'required'}` now reports a loud miss when it fired but woke
**nobody**:

```
required wake reached no awake/watching session for the addressee(s) — the
message was injected to their inbox (seen on their next natural turn) but the
recipient was not re-invoked now.
```

This is the exact gap that once made a wake *look* successful when nothing was
listening. Always-arm makes a required miss rare for fleet agents, but the
`recipient_absent` surface still catches a not-yet-armed / non-fleet / dead-handle
target. If you see it, the wake degraded to a plain inbox inject — the addressee
sees it on their next natural turn, not now.

## The one deploy-time hazard: migration 183 rides the deploy (D-012)

If you are deploying or debugging the live DB: **never manually apply migration 183
(the partial unique index) to the shared `papercusp` database.** The green-main
operator (`:3070`, the live fleet) still *plain-inserts* `coord:inbox-wake:*` rows
(no `ON CONFLICT`) until the Phase-1 upsert code is deployed. Applying the unique
index first would dedup to one row/agent and then make green-main's next idle insert
throw a `unique_violation` → live-fleet idle-arm regression.

The index is correct and applies clean empty→head; it must land **coupled with the
upsert code**, which only happens through the green-main deploy
(green-checkpoint → release-trigger → `deploy-cli applyStagedMigrations`). It is not
triggerable by accident: boot-migrate is gated off on `:3170`, and `:3070` reads the
release SQL dir. So "apply 183 to live PG" is a no-op-by-design that rides the deploy
— not a pending manual step.

## Cross-owner discovery safety (EI-151)

A wake / `turn:interrupt` resolves a peer's LIVE interactive session via
`findLiveHost(ownerId)`, which reads a discovery file at
`~/.papercusp/psu-pty/<sanitizeKey(ownerId)>.json`. `sanitizeKey` is **lossy**
(every char outside `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]` → `_`, truncated to 200), so two *distinct*
coord owner ids can resolve to the **same** filename (a structured pot id vs a
colliding one; a stale file left at a reused key during a `/loop` re-host). The
filename alone is therefore NOT proof of ownership: `findLiveHost` also requires
the file's **recorded `ownerId`** to equal the one asked for, else it returns
null (→ park/inbox, never the wrong session). Without that check, agent A's
inbox-wake (or a force-interrupt) would inject into agent B's live session — the
third member of the cross-agent-wake-misroute family (EI-152 / EI-153 / EI-151).
The guard lives in the ONE shared discovery function so it covers both the
wake-executor's `psu-socket-inject` rung and `turn:interrupt`'s pty-force leg.
Regression: `psu-pty-discovery.test.ts` "EI-151 … recorded ownerId differs from
the requested key".

### The second rung: recycled-pid managed-pty inject (EI-151, Channel 1)

The discovery-file check above guards the `psu-socket-inject` rung. The
wake-executor has an EARLIER rung — Channel 1, `findPty(pid)` — for sessions that
are one of OUR managed ptys (`/adv`-spawned). It matched on **pid alone**, but
the OS **recycles a pid** to a *different* agent's live managed pty after a
session exits uncleanly (its `adv_sessions` row never marked ended). So the
recorded pid for sleeping agent A could now belong to agent B's live pty, and A's
wake turn would inject into B's session — the same cross-agent misroute, one rung
up. Fix: `PtyHandle` captures **`ownerSid`** from `PAPERCUSP_SID` at spawn, and
`findPtyByPid(pid, ownerSid)` rejects a handle tagged with a foreign owner. An
**untagged** pty (`ownerSid === null` — a shell pane / legacy spawn) still
matches, so the guard is never *stricter* than the old pid-only behavior. The
wake-executor passes `d.subscriberId` (which is also the `PAPERCUSP_SID` it
stamps on resume), and parks on a cross-owner miss instead of injecting.
Regression: `pty-bridge.test.ts` "findPtyByPid owner-scoping" +
`wake-executor-matrix.test.ts` "EI-151 cross-owner pid-reuse". **Lesson:** any
pid→session routing must be owner-scoped — a pid is not a stable identity.

## The dual: turn-interrupt — ending a RUNNING peer's turn

Wake re-invokes a *sleeping* agent; **`turn:interrupt`** ends a *running* one's
turn. It is **operator-mediated** (D-008): every fleet agent runs as the same OS
user, so authorization / attribution / rate-limit can't live at the OS socket —
they live in the tool. `turn:interrupt { owner, mode, reason }` — `reason` is
REQUIRED and audited.

**Two modes:**

- **`cooperative`** (the polite default) — injects a high-priority `yield` coord
  message (glyph `|`) into the peer's `[coord+N]` block mid-turn. The peer follows
  the yield policy every role's prompt now carries (the dual clause to this page's
  wake guidance): reach a safe checkpoint, persist partial state to the work_item,
  release locks, write a one-line successor note, end the turn. It is **not** killed.
  It **DEFERS** when the target holds file locks (a critical section) — a hard yield
  mid-edit can orphan a lock or half-write a file, so it lets the atomic edit finish
  and the lock release first, then you retry.
- **`force`** — ends the turn NOW, mid-thinking. A managed-pty session gets Ctrl+C
  over its control socket (the Phase-3 `interruptViaPty` seam); a headless spawn gets
  SIGINT to the session pid. The **turn** ends, not the agent — the session stays
  resumable by id. On a critical section `force` WARNS (orphaned-edit hazard) but
  proceeds.

**Guardrails (D-009):** `reason` required; every call audited
(`turn.interrupt_cooperative` / `_force` / `_deferred` / `_rate_limited` / `_failed`
in `harness_shared.audit_log`); storm-limited so a confused or looping agent can't
halt the fleet. The base ceiling is `STORM_MAX` (10 / 60s / actor, the audit log is
the rate source), but `stormMaxFor(actor)` raises it for trusted SYSTEM recovery
actors that legitimately force-ESC many *distinct* owners in one burst — a
fleet-wide recovery loop was tripping the flat cap after ~10 different owners
(`gateway-mass-outage-storm-guard-2026-07-01`). Self-interrupt refused.

**Reach for cooperative first**; use `force` only when cooperative was ignored or
there's no time. To re-invoke an *idle* peer use `coord:send {wake:true}` — interrupt
is for a *running* peer. The `yield` glyph + every other line type are sourced from
the one `COORD_LEGEND`; see [the coord injection protocol](/internal/docs/agent-insights/coord-injection-protocol).

**Known gaps (2026-06-08):** the managed-pty typing-parity feel-check and the
default-on flip (`PAPERCUSP_PSU_PTY` is opt-in today), and a full live interactive
force-interrupt-mid-thinking e2e, are not yet run — the transport and the logic are
